core_obligations: Case M perfect: observe that both sides of the displayed arrow transform distinguished triangles in M into distinguished triangles and commute with direct sums, so by the check-on-a-generator remark and the classical-generator lemma it suffices to verify the statement for M = R[n], where it is obvious (proof lines 28670-28676).
Case K perfect: repeat the same generator argument with the roles of K and M interchanged (proof lines 28678-28679).

Case (3): represent K and L by bounded below complexes K^bullet and L^bullet, take K^bullet K-flat with flat terms using the tor amplitude lemma, and represent M by a bounded above complex M^bullet of finite free R-modules as pseudo-coherence permits (proof lines 28682-28688).

Identify the left-hand object as Tot(K^bullet tensor_R Hom^bullet(M^bullet, L^bullet)) and the right-hand object as Hom^bullet(M^bullet, Tot(K^bullet tensor_R L^bullet)), using the Hom-out-of-projective lemma (proof lines 28689-28697).

Observe that both complexes have in degree n the module given by the direct sum over p + q + r = n of K^p tensor Hom_R(M^{-r}, L^q), equal to the direct sum of Hom_R(M^{-r}, K^p tensor_R L^q) because M^{-r} is finite free and the sums are finite (proof lines 28698-28703).
Conclude that the map of the lemma is induced by the explicit map of complexes built from these canonical isomorphisms, which proves case (3) (proof lines 28704-28707).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R and objects K, L, M of D(R) and asserts that the map K tensor^L_R R Hom_R(M, L) -> R Hom_R(M, K tensor^L_R L) is an isomorphism in three cases: when M is perfect; when K is perfect; and when M is pseudo-coherent, L lies in D^+(R), and K has tor amplitude in [a, infinity] (source lines 28652-28667). The proof treats the first two cases by a generator reduction and the third by an explicit complex computation. In case M perfect, both sides of the arrow transform distinguished triangles in M into distinguished triangles and commute with direct sums, so by the check-on-a-generator remark and the classical-generator lemma it suffices to verify the statement for M = R[n], where it is obvious; case K perfect is settled by the same argument with the roles of the two arguments interchanged (proof lines 28670-28679). Case (3) is the substantive computation: the proof represents K and L by bounded below complexes K^bullet and L^bullet, may take K^bullet K-flat with flat terms by the tor amplitude lemma, and represents M by a bounded above complex M^bullet of finite free modules as pseudo-coherence allows (proof lines 28682-28688). It then identifies the object on the left as Tot(K^bullet tensor_R Hom^bullet(M^bullet, L^bullet)) and the object on the right as Hom^bullet(M^bullet, Tot(K^bullet tensor_R L^bullet)), using the Hom-out-of-projective lemma, and observes that both complexes have in degree n the same module, namely the direct sum over p + q + r = n of K^p tensor Hom_R(M^{-r}, L^q), identified with the direct sum of Hom_R(M^{-r}, K^p tensor_R L^q) because M^{-r} is finite free and the sums are finite (proof lines 28689-28703). The map of the lemma is then the one induced by the explicit map of complexes whose components are these canonical isomorphisms (proof lines 28704-28707). The non-routine content is the generator reduction in the perfect cases and the degreewise identification in case (3).
